s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
Lip edema with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped-up margins
key_facts: 34-year-old African American man
Hemophilia A
HIV-1 infection
Hepatitis C virus infection
3-month history of intermittent fever and unintentional weight loss
Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
CD4 count rose from 94 to 160 cells/mm3 after resuming antiretroviral therapy
Lip lesions developed approximately two months after CD4 count began to improve
No hepatosplenomegaly
Undetectable HIV viral load
Undetectable hepatitis C viral load
Negative polymerase-chain-reaction assay for herpes simplex virus
Normal complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels
Negative Gram stain, acid-fast stain, and mucicarmine stain of lesion samples

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with HIV-1 infection and lip lesions

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with intermittent fever and weight loss

shortlist.label: Cheilitis granulomatosa
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations

shortlist.label: Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring lip swelling and ulcerations in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with intermittent fever and weight loss, and possible granulomatous disease

raw.rationale: The patient's HIV-1 infection, improvement in CD4 count, and development of lip lesions with painful ulcerations are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, which is a common malignancy in immunocompromised individuals, particularly those with HIV/AIDS.

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Negative fungal blood cultures and negative urine and serum Histoplasma antigen tests

rejected.label: Cheilitis granulomatosa
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic granulomatous inflammation and systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome
rejected.why: Absence of facial paralysis, Bell's palsy, and lack of typical recurrent facial edema

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: No evidence of granulomatous disease, hepatosplenomegaly, or other systemic symptoms
